title: Turnip greens, fresh, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Turnip greens are the leafy tops of the turnip plant, commonly used as a vegetable. When cooked with added fat the leaves stay bright green, become tender, and retain a mildly bitter flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnip greens belong to the cruciferous family, like broccoli and cabbage.
The leaves are rich in chlorophyll, giving them a deep green color.
In traditional Southern US cuisine they are often prepared as “collard greens” with bacon or ham.
Turnip greens contain more vitamin K than spinach.
They can be used in soups, stews, and as a side dish.

items.title: High in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for normal blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of vitamins A and C
items.content: These vitamins support vision, immunity, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and especially beneficial during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie fiber source
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Glucosinolates and carotenoids help combat free radicals.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Turnip greens contain oxalates, which may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, people allergic to other cruciferous vegetables may react to turnip greens.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Cooking with added fat increases calorie density; monitor the amount of oil or meat used.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Turnip greens are typically simmered in a small amount of fat (oil, bacon) until tender, often with onion and garlic. They can also be quickly sautéed or added to soups and stews. Serve hot as a side dish or cooled in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh leaves in the refrigerator in a perforated bag for 3‑5 days. Cooked turnip greens can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
